items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: It started out Clark Terry and Bobby Graf from St. Louis, a tenor player, myself on front line... And then Bobby Graf left shortly after we organized

ctx.x: It started out Clark Terry and Bobby Graf from St. Louis, a tenor player, myself on front line, Bill Basie and Jimmy Lewis played bass and Gus Johnson played drums. And shortly after that, Freddie Green joined and that was fantastic. It really made that group.
You had to have Freddie, right?

items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: For instance, when he organized the first group the tenor player was not Wardell, it was Bobby Graf from St. Louis, a white guy by the way. He didn’t stay long, I don’t know what happened, but he didn’t stay long

ctx.x: Because all the rest of those players, weren’t they from Basie’s band, most of them?

No. No. Not all of them. For instance, when he organized the first group the tenor player was not Wardell, it was Bobby Graf from St. Louis, a white guy by the way. He didn’t stay long, I don’t know what happened, but he didn’t stay long, and Wardell Gray came in, who was a great player also. I liked Wardell, and a brilliant guy, well read.
And I think I read somewhere that you said that your impression of Basie was that he was one of the sort of old-timers who really appreciated a modern conception of music.
